title: Four append-only JSONL journals re-solve torn-tail, rollback and latching independently
note: Overstated. jobstore (store.go:779-806) and delegatestore (store.go:235-262) do share the truncate+seek+sync rollback and unusable latch, with small differences (jobstore seeks EOF and invalidates its cursor; delegatestore seeks to offset). sessionlog does NOT: grep of sessionlog.go finds no rollback, truncate, sync, unusable or closed latch; it only tracks tornTail and writes a separator (lines 179-195). transcript.go has a much richer protocol (ErrRollbackFailed, positionUnknown, append tail, batches) that is not a copy of the others. Torn-tail policies diverge on purpose per file. The proposed generic journal Appender over four stores with durability code is high risk for ~two real copies.
revised_fix_plan: Limit scope to jobstore and delegatestore: extract one small rollback-to-offset helper plus latch if Jesse wants it; leave sessionlog and transcript alone. Needs design discussion first; run on CI only.

title: jobstore fold cache is four copies of one pattern and three overlapping caching layers
note: Verified: store.go:862-939 four hit/note pairs identical in shape; cloneFoldJobs (945-966) and cloneFoldOrdered (968-988) copy the same 8-field JobRecord block; foldcache.go package comment 'mirrors' fileCursor; delegatestore loadLocked (store.go:58-76) re-reads and re-folds every call. But a generic cachedFold[T] is awkward because folds.gen is shared across all four and each projection has its own clone, so saving is closer to 40-50 lines, not 90. The clearly worthwhile piece is the duplicated clone block.
revised_fix_plan: Extract cloneJobRecord used by both cloners (certain win). Only add generics if the shared gen field stays correct; skip delegatestore.Load changes without measurement. Shorten foldcache's mirroring commentary.

title: artifactstore redundant chmods and path-bearing ref map
note: Store.go:34 Chmod after MkdirTemp and :68 Chmod after WriteFile exist, and refs maps ref->path where path is always filepath.Join(dir,id). But the chmods are not strictly redundant: MkdirTemp/WriteFile modes are masked by umask, so a restrictive umask could leave unusable perms; the chmod guarantees 0700/0600. Missing doc comments confirmed. Cosmetic.
revised_fix_plan: Add doc comments; optionally make refs a set. Keep the chmods.
